body:
In the MRP, `GameSocket` is never initialized, so disposing throws a `NullReferenceException` which seems to match the errors you're seeing.

Managed objects such as `GameSocket` should be disposed only when `disposing` is `true`, as per the [documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/garbage-collection/implementing-dispose). You should also check if `GameSocket` is `null`. As per the [guidelines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/design-guidelines/dispose-pattern) you should avoid throwing exceptions within a `Dispose` method.

We generally try to avoid editor crashes, but catching exceptions during Mono domain finalization isn't possible. This process calls the object finalizers which in turn calls the `Dispose` method with `dispose` set to `false`.

We finalize the domain when the C# project is rebuilt to reload your project's assembly. This is necessary because we need to execute `[Tool]` scripts that run in the editor, and to retrieve default property values, etc.

Unfortunately, I don't think there's anything we can do on our side. The assembly reloading mechanism should be more robust in Godot 4, because ALC reloading is a more cooperative process.
